issues.title: Fix Free-Threading support
issues.body:
Current `msgspec` has lots of places with FT bug, data races, missing atomics, etc.
We need to fix them, so `msgspec` would work on FT builds correctly.

However, we **must not** make `msgspec` slower on regular GIL builds.

This is a meta-issue, report your findings here, propose tooling and CI improvements.
issues.author: sobolevn

comments.body:

We *really* should figure out some reliable, continuous benchmarking solution. However, I'm currently out of ideas, short of spinning up ephemeral VMs on a dedicated machine.

comments.body:
Findings from TSAN and stress testing on a free-threaded build
I've been testing msgspec on free-threaded CPython 3.14t using the TSAN image from nascheme/cpython_sanity, with msgspec built using -fsanitize=thread and assertions enabled.
My fork: https://github.com/Tapanhaz/msgspec
The existing test suite produces no TSAN reports, but a separate stress suite that releases multiple threads simultaneously onto shared objects exposes several issues:
1. Union decoding uses an uninitialized StructInfo. Concurrent first use of shared Struct types can result in a NULL TypeNode (assert(type != NULL) in json_decode_struct_map_inner). I have a candidate fix using a StructInfo_wait_initialized() helper that is a no-op on GIL builds: [fix-union-structinfo-wait](https://github.com/Tapanhaz/msgspec/tree/ft/fix-union-structinfo-wait).
2. JSON and msgpack dict encoding can produce corrupt output during concurrent mutation. Both read the dict length before entering the critical section. If the dict is emptied in between, JSON can overwrite its opening { with }, while msgpack can write a header count that doesn't match the number of items encoded. I have a candidate fix that encodes a PyDict_Copy snapshot on free-threaded builds, leaving GIL builds unchanged: [fix-dict-encode-snapshot](https://github.com/Tapanhaz/msgspec/tree/ft/fix-dict-encode-snapshot).
3. Other potential stale-length and borrowed-reference issues, similar to the crash fixed in #1252, appear in json_encode_sequence, encode_lines, to_builtins_list, convert_seq_to_list, and struct slot reads (Struct_get_index_noerror). I have TSAN reports and stack traces for these. A PyList_GetSlice snapshot may be an alternative to lock-and-recheck for lists.
4. A separate bug also affects GIL builds. A failed conversion involving mutually recursive types can leave partially constructed type information cached. A subsequent Decoder(B) may then succeed, and decoding can segfault. I reproduced this on 0.22.0 and will file it separately with a reproducer.
I'm also preparing a report-only TSAN CI job so these issues can be investigated without blocking CI: [TSAN CI branch](https://github.com/Tapanhaz/msgspec/tree/ci/tsan).
comments.author: Tapanhaz

issues.title: Segfault reading decimal_format after a failed Encoder.__init__ re-call
issues.body:
### Description

If an encoder was created with a callable `decimal_format` and `__init__` is then called again on it with an invalid `decimal_format`, the `ValueError` is raised but the encoder is left half reset. Reading `enc.decimal_format` afterwards crashes the interpreter with a segfault, and encoding a `Decimal` raises `SystemError`. This happens with both `msgspec.json.Encoder` and `msgspec.msgpack.Encoder`.

Minimal example (the crash itself):

```python
import msgspec

enc = msgspec.json.Encoder(decimal_format=str)
try:
    enc.__init__(decimal_format="bad")
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)
print(enc.decimal_format)  # Segmentation fault
```

Script that runs each case in a child process so it can report the return code:

```python
import subprocess
import sys

CASES = {
    "json: read decimal_format": (
        "import msgspec\n"
        "enc = msgspec.json.Encoder(decimal_format=str)\n"
        "try:\n"
        "    enc.__init__(decimal_format='bad')\n"
        "except ValueError as e:\n"
        "    print('ValueError:', e, flush=True)\n"
        "print(enc.decimal_format)\n"
    ),
    "msgpack: read decimal_format": (
        "import msgspec\n"
        "enc = msgspec.msgpack.Encoder(decimal_format=str)\n"
        "try:\n"
        "    enc.__init__(decimal_format='bad')\n"
        "except ValueError as e:\n"
        "    print('ValueError:', e, flush=True)\n"
        "print(enc.decimal_format)\n"
    ),
    "json: encode Decimal": (
        "import decimal, msgspec\n"
        "enc = msgspec.json.Encoder(decimal_format=str)\n"
        "try:\n"
        "    enc.__init__(decimal_format='bad')\n"
        "except ValueError as e:\n"
        "    print('ValueError:', e, flush=True)\n"
        "print(enc.encode(decimal.Decimal('1')))\n"
    ),
    "msgpack: encode Decimal": (
        "import decimal, msgspec\n"
        "enc = msgspec.msgpack.Encoder(decimal_format=str)\n"
        "try:\n"
        "    enc.__init__(decimal_format='bad')\n"
        "except ValueError as e:\n"
        "    print('ValueError:', e, flush=True)\n"
        "print(enc.encode(decimal.Decimal('1')))\n"
    ),
}

for name, code in CASES.items():
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60
    )
    print(f"== {name}")
    print(proc.stdout.rstrip())
    err = proc.stderr.strip().splitlines()
    if err:
        print("stderr:", err[-1])
    print("returncode:", proc.returncode)
    print()
```

Output:

```
== json: read decimal_format
ValueError: `decimal_format` must be 'string', 'number', or a callable, got 'bad'
returncode: -11

== msgpack: read decimal_format
ValueError: `decimal_format` must be 'string', 'number', or a callable, got 'bad'
returncode: -11

== json: encode Decimal
ValueError: `decimal_format` must be 'string', 'number', or a callable, got 'bad'
stderr: SystemError: null argument to internal routine
returncode: 1

== msgpack: encode Decimal
ValueError: `decimal_format` must be 'string', 'number', or a callable, got 'bad'
stderr: SystemError: null argument to internal routine
returncode: 1
```

Return code -11 is SIGSEGV.

Expected: the failed `__init__` raises `ValueError` and leaves the encoder in a consistent state, so `decimal_format` returns a value and encoding a `Decimal` works (or at least raises a normal Python error). It should never crash the process.

Versions: Python 3.12.3, msgspec 0.22.0, Linux.

Cause (`src/msgspec/_core.c` at 96cff1e): `Encoder_init` clears `self->decimal_callable = NULL` unconditionally at line 9839, before validating the new value. The invalid-value branch (lines 9860-9867) raises and returns -1 without touching `self->decimal_format`, so it still says `DECIMAL_FORMAT_CALLABLE` from the first init while the callable pointer is now NULL. `Encoder_decimal_format` then does `Py_INCREF(self->decimal_callable)` on the NULL at line 10154, and `mpack_encode_decimal` (line 13652) and `json_encode_decimal` (line 14316) pass the NULL to `PyObject_CallFunctionObjArgs`. Both encoder types use this `tp_init` (lines 13920 and 15155).

Proposed fix: parse and validate `decimal_format` into locals first, and only once it is valid assign `self->decimal_format` and replace `self->decimal_callable` with `Py_XSETREF`, so a failed re-init leaves the previous state intact. `Py_XSETREF` also releases the old callable on a successful re-init, which the current plain assignment never does. A regression test would call `__init__` again with `"bad"` and then read `decimal_format` and encode a `Decimal`.

I'm happy to open a PR with the fix and the test.
issues.author: digit50

comments.body: How did you come up with this? Calling `__init__` by hand outside a `super()` call is rather unorthodox, and I'm not sure there's any guarantee you'll get a useful result here.
comments.author: provinzkraut

comments.body: I was reading the validation added for the callable `decimal_format` and noticed `decimal_callable` is cleared before the new value is checked, so I tried a failing re-init to see what state it leaves. Agreed that calling `__init__` again is unusual. The concern is only that a failing `__init__` leaves the encoder in a state that segfaults on attribute access. If re-init is not meant to be supported, a clear error on a second call would also close it.
comments.author: digit50
provinzkraut
